lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 12:00 UTC on 10 September to 11:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 18 with the mode trend-down and peaks immediately at 24 in the 13:00 UTC slot on 10 September, spanning that day's cash open, the only slot in the whole window mapped to WATCH and still one point below the block threshold. Tail then decayed to 17 and 14 as price discovery stayed orderly, held a 14 to 19 band through the afternoon with the mode mixed, and recorded event/whipsaw at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC normalised into an 11 to 15 band with mixed conditions, the quietest stretch of the window. The final six slots from 06:00 UTC record trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14, 15 and 14 as the overnight advance extended, stalled beneath its high, gave back part of the move and was then bought back. Stress never left the extreme band, running 81 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held 85 to 89 throughout, so the evidence base was consistently strong until the unverified release outcome of the current hour.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the remainder of the 11 September session and then spends fifteen of its twenty-four slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 21 in the current slot, which contains the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report whose actual and post-release path are not verified at this assessment time. The window peak is 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the amplifier and a first genuine retracement the rejection. Both slots are inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and they are the only two slots mapped to WATCH. The path then steps down through 19 across the preliminary Michigan release, 17, 16 and 15 through the midday lull on the assumption that volatility decays and two-way range behaviour returns, holds 15 across the 18:00 UTC budget statement, lifts to 16 and then 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly rebalancing flow concentrates, and falls to a 5 to 6 floor for the closure hours. That floor represents residual gap risk into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen rather than any intraday mechanism, and the flatness across those slots is a property of a closed venue rather than forecast conviction. Stress stays extreme through the release and the cash open at 88 and 90, leaves the extreme band by 16:00 UTC and decays through elevated into moderate across the closure. Confidence eases from 70 to 40 as the horizon moves past the last observable quote.

body:
The decisive fact this hour is a timing one. The August consumer price report was released at 12:30 UTC, four to six minutes before this assessment, and no primary or secondary source consulted had published a verified actual by the assessment cutoff. The Bureau of Labor Statistics release page still served the July report transmitted on 12 August, the structured economic calendar still showed the August rows as awaiting release, and no wire story carrying the outcome was retrievable. This assessment therefore contains no claim about what the report said and no claim about how price responded to it.

What is observed is the state the market carried into the release. Two independent feeds agree that NQ traded 29,337.50, up 202.25 points or 0.69% against a 29,135.25 previous close, at 12:16 to 12:17 UTC. The session high was 29,339.75 and price sat within three points of it. That is a change from the previous hour, when price had eased roughly forty-six points below the same high and the retracement was read as granted. The pullback has since been bought back and price re-approached the extreme without the high itself extending. Holding near a session extreme into a scheduled release is a genuine amplifier, and it is the principal reason tail lifts from 14 to 21.

Tail at 21 sits in the watch band, four points below the 25 block threshold, and it is deliberately held there rather than pushed higher. The distinction that matters is between a large move and a pathological price path. A surprise in either direction can produce a violent but orderly repricing in which retracements are still granted, and a mean-reversion mechanism tolerates that. What it does not tolerate is persistent one-way extension after failed pullbacks. None of that has been observed, because nothing at all has been observed since the print. Raising tail through the block threshold on an unobserved outcome would be scoring the importance of the event rather than the structure of the path, which the published risk definition explicitly separates.

Cross-asset evidence continues to withhold confirmation of a melt-up or a breakdown. VIX is 17.04, down 4.48% and near the low of a 17.04 to 17.71 band. The ten-year yield is 4.957%, up 1.3 basis points from a 4.944% previous close and mid-range between 4.936% and 4.978%; the thirty-year remains above 5.3%. WTI is $99.29, down 3.12%, and Brent $104.39, down 3.01%, after the International Energy Agency projected a 2026 supply surplus. Falling crude into an inflation print measurably reduces the near-term energy impulse. Delayed cross-asset context collected at 11:51 UTC shows Nasdaq futures up 0.63%, the volatility contract down 3.74% and Treasury futures essentially unchanged, which is directionally consistent with the live quotes without adding independent price-path information.

Breadth context points one way and is treated with the caution its provenance requires. All seven tracked semiconductors and seven of eight megacaps were positive on a latest-session basis, with the semiconductor mean at 0.98% and the megacap mean at 0.44%. That is aligned, and alignment is one of the named amplifiers. It is also explicitly non-real-time, carries no source as-of stamp, and describes the prior session rather than the current path, so it supports the trend-up reading of the pre-release hours without being allowed to establish current structure on its own.

Stress rises six points to 88 and stays extreme. The environment is genuinely difficult and independent of the path question. A global bond selloff has carried the ten-year toward 5%, the long end is pressured by supply, crude sits near $100 on an unresolved Middle East conflict with a naval blockade constraining Iranian exports, the major averages fell through the week with the Nasdaq down roughly 1.6% since Monday, equity funds recorded heavy outflows, and futures pricing implied a substantial probability that the 16 September policy decision delivers a rate increase rather than a hold. Thursday's producer price report ran slightly hotter than expected. An inflation print landing into that configuration is a high-stress moment by construction, which is precisely what the stress score is for and precisely what it must not be allowed to do to the tail score.

Confidence is 70, solid, down from 89. The evidence base is broad: two agreeing live futures feeds, a real-time volatility index, real-time two-year and ten-year yields, both crude benchmarks, a verified seven-day calendar and fresh cross-asset context. Against that sits one material blind spot at the single most decision-relevant moment of the week. That is a genuine and specific gap rather than thin or stale evidence generally, so confidence falls to the middle of the solid band rather than into the low band.

The forward path treats the next two hours as the conditional peak and then decays. The 13:00 UTC slot spanning the 13:30 UTC cash open holds 22, the highest value in the window, because the opening auction is the first structure that could either confirm a post-release move through shallow pullbacks and repeated extension or reject it through a first genuine retracement. From 14:00 UTC the path steps down to 19, 17, 16 and 15 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly and volatility decays, lifts modestly to 16 and then 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly rebalancing concentrates, and falls to a 5 to 6 floor once CME equity futures close at 21:00 UTC. Fifteen of the twenty-four forward slots fall inside that weekend closure, where the floor represents residual reopen gap risk rather than any intraday mechanism. Two slots are mapped to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold.
